## Claims
- [source-backed] Inspected alternate-provider full text: ar5iv’s rendering of St. Dizier–Yong, DOI 10.1112/jlms.12832, supplied with SHA-256 `6066dee1db75213a13ca9c407c8944c09c7391fb0fb69f1d4a386ed4292fc456`. It identifies the 2011 Reiner–Woo–Yong paper separately as reference [12]. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 548-550]
- [source-backed] The supplied rendering contains visibly corrupted required material: after introducing (8) and (9), it truncates mathematical content, and Definition 2.1 reads only “valid if \(n,r,i,j,a,b,N\ge1\) with \(r\ 9)\),” omitting its inequalities. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 149-164]
- [source-backed] The visible linkage is: Lemma 2.5 says a specified nonzero homogeneous syzygy implies consistency of decomposable equations (10); Theorem 4.4 declares the corresponding system inconsistent when wide right sides vanish and some tall right side is nonzero; Theorem 4.5 invokes Lemma 2.5 and Theorem 4.4. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 176-190] [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 473-502]
- [source-backed] In Theorem 4.4, “\(N\le\min(j,n-r-i)\)” is proof-case-specific, not a theorem hypothesis: the theorem begins “For any valid \(\varphi\),” and its proof subsequently treats both \(N\le\min(j,n-r-i)\) and \(N>\min(j,n-r-i)\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 473-486]
- [proved] The requested source certificate is **not established** from the supplied record: the only alternate-provider full text is corrupted precisely where complete equations (8)–(10) and Definition 2.1’s valid-tuple inequalities are required. Hence neither the visible linkage nor adjacent 2011-paper identification can substitute for one uncorrupted bounded source-29 excerpt.

## Strategy
Compared the supplied alternate-provider full text against every required component and separated Theorem 4.4’s stated “valid” hypothesis from its proof-local \(N\)-case split.

## Gaps
No supplied uncorrupted bounded passage gives the full text of equations (8)–(10) or all Definition 2.1 inequalities. No further alternate-provider full text is supplied.

## Next
Obtain a new bounded, hashed full-text extraction preserving Definition 2.1 and equations (8)–(10).
